The metal frame feels solid but light, and the spring hinges contain just the right amount of tension. There are no crude screws holding the lenses in place, hidden from the people around you by resting fractions of an inch from your skin, and the lenses themselves produce no obvious distortion.

Unless said lenses prove far more prone to scratching than currently seem to be the case, I will hang on to these for a while; should I lose them, I’ll be quick to grab another pair. They were dinged a star only because the nosepieces were slightly bent upon arrival, and I had to carefully, nervously twist them back into place with a pair of pliers.

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Mini Putt Golf Game for Kids - Spin n' Putt Electronic Putting Game - Indoor Mini Golf for Kids + Toddlers - Putter + Balls Included The Franklin spin n putt golf game is a pretty cool game. It comes with a base (with ramp), flag, 10 plastic golf balls, and a plastic/metal putter. The foot pedal is used to start and stop the spinning motion of the base. There are 10 holes/slots for the golf balls to land in with points ranging from 5 to 100. 5 of the 10 balls are white and the other 5 are yellow. Once you decide who goes first he or she will putt all 5 balls toward the base. Anything not in a slot counts as 0 points. After player one shoots player 2 gets to shoot his or her 5 balls. Clearly, you are able to make up your own game and rules.  The one thing I like about this set is that there is no putting green strip. Therefore you are able to putt from any angle or even try to bounce off a wall and into the slots. text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

I've used the light as a headlamp while camping and don't like it much for that. The headband is very uncomfortable since there's no cushion on the mounting bracket. I'm left with a sore indentation on my forehead. The light also does not tilt like a good headlamp should.

text_fidelity_a: Portable Dual Burner Alcohol Stove Alcohol Heater Burner with Glass Kettle for Tea Coffee Maker Outdoor Backpacking Picnic Camping Hiking Korean BBQ I live in Texas and in the February blizzard we had last year, I was stuck in my home without power for 5 days.  20 degrees outside, it was around 34 inside...for 5 days.  I did turn on my water faucets so that my pipes did not freeze and burst, and I was lucky enough to have a loaf of bread, peanut butter & jelly, and powdered milk.  So, in the months and months since then, I have gotten solar panels, a 200 amp hour LifePO4 battery, a 3000 watt inverter...but also have camp stoves run with propane, a propane heater and now this really nice little alcohol burner.  I also have a couple of mini-firepits that use 99% alcohol for fuel which is what this little burner uses as well.  I can at least boil water on this little burner with the power out, but with the included screen, it can be used outside as well (with the screen keeping any breeze from causing a problem).  When wondering how long you may be in the dark during a power outage, having a couple of solar lights and a way to heat up soup or make coffee on this little burner gives me peace of mind.  I love the carry case - I do have a propane cook stove that has a carrier and that makes it easy to store them both for the next time I need to use them.  I do think the price is a bit high, but again, having "redundancy" in emergency situations is important to me and I'm happy with adding this burner to my emergency use for heating food/drinks.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Dual Burner Alcohol Stove Alcohol Heater Burner with Glass Kettle for Tea Coffee Maker Outdoor Backpacking Picnic Camping Hiking Korean BBQ

Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2) I've owned this brand and style of water container for almost 17 years, it's my go-to for camping and day trips where there might not be any water. I have almost always had at least 2 of them, one for drinking water, the other for potable water (cleaning dishes, cooking, dog water). Recently having to purchase two more, I guess the one that's put on the age and seen places finally developed a crack on the bottom. Not bad after 7-8 years being lugged around.

Pros: Lots of water on hand - Easy to use - Stack able - Durable - Trusted brand -

Cons: Heavy once full (7gallons x 7lbs per gallon of water + container = 50lbs) - spigot almost never lines up pointing down no matter how many ways you screw on the cap - price raised by $10 in past year

Points to look at when choosing: If you can't lift 7 gallons, get the 2.5 or 5 gallon model
(Here is an example per the National Park Service) 2 gallons a day per person when camping, you can figure the same if the water at your house is shut off during a emergency event. You might add an extra gallon for toilet flushes.
text_fidelity_b: Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2)

We were blown away by the weight, but then talked about it and not having thought about it, realized this would increase safety as you stand and squat down onto these things. Okay, so heavy, check. I have only used them at with the two pieces, not one, so we'll play with them and see. It IS sturdy up to the listed weight capacity and it is stable on the floor. Some assembly is required. The 'parts' come nicely wrapped and shrink wrapped nuts, bolts and washers kept the project in order while I was putting things together. My unit came with holes matching up nicely: it is always a good idea to leave the fasteners a little loose until the pieces are all fitted together, since some nudging is almost always required at some point to achieve a proper alignment. Be sure to tighten things then. I do NOT have a matching set of hand weights so I was interesting to see how well/IF the shorter, lighter weights would fit on the rack as I hoped. My SHORTEST weight is a 4 LB 'Yes4All' coated vinyl number, 6 3/4-inches end-to-end and it just fits securely on the rack. Shorter length weights would fall through the front and back rails any way you can install the rails.

I keep my weights and rack in a large walk-in closet where the rack fits under the clothes bars. I only have a few weights here but I have found that the bottom rails work fine as a shoe rack. Now both the weights and the shoes are being kept in good order.

Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards I ordered this item to have a handy way to inflate a slam ball after they lose air over time. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. However, this little unit worked incredibly well.

It charges quickly via USB Micro (120 minutes to full charge / with 30 inflates per charge), has all of the accessories needed to get going (USB cable, air needles, attachment hose, etc..), has pre-set modes for a football, a soccer ball, a basketball, etc.. And is super compact & lightweight (6.29" x 1.4" & weighing only 6.5oz).

I haven't tried, but don't see why you couldn't even inflate a bicycle tire with this unit as well. However, I probably wouldn't try with anything larger like a car or truck tire out of concern of damaging the pump.

There is an auto-shut off option (IE: when you use a ball preset the pump will turn off when it dispenses the appropriate amount of air for the selected ball), however, there is no pressure gauge. So, if you don't use the preset, then you have to go by feel (or have an air gauge on hand).

As far as my experiment, I didn't even use the presets. Just popped in the needle into my slam ball & turned on the pump. It inflated (my very deflated) slam ball in a matter of seconds. A success!

If you're constantly using a foot pump or bike pump to inflate your sports equipment, bike tires, etc.., then seriously consider this portable pump instead. Makes this process super easy. There's even an attachment that looks like it's to be used for blowing up balloons! Very cool!
text_fidelity_b: Morpilot 20PSI Paddle Board Pump - Dual Stage Inflation with Powerful SUP Pump Inflator & Deflator, Auto-Off, AC & DC, Intelligent Preset - Perfect for Inflatable Stand-Up Paddle Boards

text_fidelity_a:
Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper This is made of a light, soft, flame retardant flannel.

It has a long white zipper which goes almost to the toes, with an easy snap at the top.

The fabric is cute with Patriots logo.

It has white stitching for accent.

It is 100% polyester. I prefer cotton which breathes better.

It has two pesky labels at the top back.

You are supposed to turn this inside out when you wash on cold, gentle cycle with like colors. Do not use fabric softener or it will impact flame retardant ability. Non-chlorine bleach. Tumble dry low.

It was made in Bangladesh.

Suggestions for improvement: use more cotton in fabric, substitute print for labels at upper back, and perhaps skip the flame retardant chemicals. 3.5 stars

Here's some info which discourages flame retardant fabrics close to children's skin:
A study published in August 2014 found that PBDEs (polybrominated diphenyl ethers), the most commonly used fire-retardant chemicals, were linked to numerous health problems.

Researchers found the chemicals were to blame for:

thyroid disruption
early onset of puberty
cognitive problems
delayed mental and physical development
“The chemicals used to make pajamas and other consumer products flame-retardant show up in water, wildlife, and human breast milk,” says pediatrician Michael Macknin, MD.

According to Dr. Macknin, the chemicals in fire retardants do diminish the flammability of products treated with them and have been associated with decreased burn injuries in children. However, the chemicals aren’t well-bound to the fabric fibers at times and can leech out. This allows the fire-retardant chemicals to float free in the environment.

“The long-term impact these chemicals may have on health and cognition is not closely scrutinized,” says Dr. Macknin. “They are often put on the market without long-term studies of their safety.”

Other dangers besides pajamas
These chemicals are found in furniture and mattresses as well as cell phones, television remotes and numerous other consumer plastics, says Dr. Macknin.

“If the tag on a sofa or mattress you’re planning to buy says, ‘this article complies with flammability requirements of California Bureau of Home Furnishings Technical Bulletin 117’, or language to that effect, it likely contains pounds of PBDEs,” he says.

You’ll find this sort of notice on numerous children’s products like car seats, strollers, toys and changing mats. According to Dr. Macknin and other health experts, these added chemicals may put your child at a greater risk than the flames they claim to inhibit. An alternative to chemically treated flame-retardant pajamas are close-fitting pajamas made of natural fibers. Some fabrics meet smolder standards without added chemicals.
text_fidelity_b: Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper

text_fidelity_a:
Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range

text_fidelity_a:
Timbuk2 Espionage Camera Backpack, Black, Medium [[VIDEOID:13357c08e01ba23329875fbdce8b14b2]] Why I chose this bag:

-I wanted a backpack instead of an over-the-shoulder case because I find that a backpack is far more comfortable when walking long distances
-I was specifically looking for a case that had space for a laptop as well as non-camera related items. When I'm taking the bag with me on a plane I don't want to fully lose one of my carry-on bags to camera equipment. Further, given that this will be the bag I'm storing underneath the seat in front of me, it needs to have space to hold whatever I might want easy access to during the flight, such as a water bottle, food, books, iPad, magazines, jacket, phone charger, etc. Most of the backpack camera bags I looked at had suprsingly little room for non-camera equipment (except for a laptop).

The attached video gives a good idea of how much the bag can hold -- I've loaded it up and then unpacked it.

Pros:

-Tough, rugged construction. No doubt that it can take a beating and protect my camera.
-Even with a large body camera it should be able to hold three lenses (not including the lends attached to the camera).
-Holds laptop and has a good amount of space for non-camera equipment.
-Comes with rain cover; can hold tripod.

Cons:

-Most of the accessory pockets are ridiculously small. For example, the pocket meant for cell phones can barely fit an iPhone 5.

Overall I think this is an excellent bag, but the MSRP price is pretty steep. If it wasn't for the fact that I was able to get the bag for 40% off the MSRP thanks to a one day sale, I would have purchased one of Timbuk2's cheaper camera bags, such as the [[ASIN:B00AMXVKLI Sleuth]] or [[ASIN:B004VD7QU4 Snoop]]. Despite the high price, I'm still going to give the Espionage five starts because it is such a well made camera bag.
text_fidelity_b: Timbuk2 Espionage Camera Backpack, Black, Medium

text_fidelity_a:
EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.
text_fidelity_b: EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App

Rubbermaid Victory Jug, 2 Gallon, Modern Red FG153004MODRD We debated whether to buy this water jug or another, more sturdy jug by another manufacturer for more than twice the money. We decided to buy the other jug when we found the Rubbermaid on sale at a local store for less than 1/3rd the cost of the more sturdy jug. For the difference in price we thought we'd give the Rubbermaid a try to see how it would perform.

The lower spigot on the Rubbermaid is solid. No leaks and easy to use. The upper vent spigot is a little bit of a weak point. It works absolutely fine, just remember to always close it so it doesn't get broken or let hot air cycle into the cold interior of the jug.

Although not an "extreme" cooler jug, once filled with ice and water we had cold water well into the second day in the desert. The cooler was kept in the shade the entire time.

If you need a rough and tumble water jug, look elsewhere. If you need something that will sit on a picnic table for a day or two, this will work fine.
text_fidelity_b: Rubbermaid Victory Jug, 2 Gallon, Modern Red FG153004MODRD

text_fidelity_a:
Kettler Travel Tour Set Pannier Set Two very handsome collapsible grocery-bag panniers, highly water resistant if not classified as waterproof, & an "overnighter" sized suitcase.
I cannot verify the stated 57 liter capacity of this set-up. I can testify that my measurements came to 51.5 liters, thereabouts. A standard large grocery bag is 6.5 inches by 11.5 inches...then there's the length...these panniers are 11/11.5 inches high. Doing the math comes to 1719 cubic inches for the pair...more of less.
The suitcase measures 19 by 12.5 by 6. so that's 1425 cu. in. Add it to the panniers comes to 3144 cu. in. or 51.5 liters.
Aside from this little discrepancy about capacity this is a well made good looking carrier system. You can toss the suitcase in the closet and still have a competent set of pannier bags that will attach to any rack. And you can still plunk your rack-bag of choice on top. I think they were called trunk bags also. Kettler took the terminology out to the proper dimensions by designing the suitcase. Velcro plus buckles hold it on top.
The panniers come collapsed inside the suitcase. All you need do is slide the ends of the plastic stays away from the thread band...you don't need to cut the thread...you can leave it in place, and then tuck the plastic ends all around the inside the pannier. And wah lah a firm & rigid pannier body all around. I did say good looking? How waterproof I don't know. No instructions. We're on our own.
I wanted a set-up like this some time ago. My delema is getting six loaves of bread home. Light but lots of volume. This system seemed the way to go. But the original price stunk. Once again Amazon to the rescue. Thanks one more time Amazon. And thanks as well for the price for the "trunk" bag from Topeak as well!
text_fidelity_b: Kettler Travel Tour Set Pannier Set

text_fidelity_a:
A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack I gave the A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack (In black) 5 stars as you can see.

Here is my situation. I hunt. Don't find much but I hunt a lot and I have this big professional camo honkering GREAT backpack. I could survive everything but a nuclear war with only that thing. And that's a good thing...but...

I also often hunt out of a portable tree stand and that big old pro back unit is just a mess in that situation. Clunky, And it's heavy! So I was really looking forward to my new backpack for the purpose. I moved the essentials from my pro pack to the new one and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack is a baby backpack for sure. It's a dufflebag put together in the shape of a backpack actually. When you get it stuffed it becomes the backpack. It has a front pocket. A mesh side pocket, good for a bottle of water or necessary paper..whatever you like. And the interior, at least for my purposes is plenty roomy. I have room to spare. That surprised me. Unlike the big boys this little pack adds zero weight to whatever you put in there. That's a bonus. The zippers worked fine, btw. Backstraps are adjustable. A little flimsy compared to high dollar, but they don't slip

Is it rough and tumble? Probably not. I wouldn't trust it in rough country with briars and such...but for normal use, it's fine. It is a day hiker or a day hunter. From the cost point and utility it's a fine choice for normal wear. I'm very pleased.
text_fidelity_b: A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack

BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift [[VIDEOID:2187373aca733f879c0dd8e6a9bc255]] This a fun headlamp designed primarily for kids who like dinosaurs and adventure.

The LED lamp is housed inside a rather large plastic T. rex head. You turn it on by squeezing the open jaws together slightly. The moderately bright light comes on, the eyes light up red, and the dinosaur makes several loud roaring sounds (see attached video). Another squeeze of the jaws and the light turns off.

The adjusable headstrap is decorated with stylized reptilian footprints, in a color scheme that suggests lizard scales. There's a strap down the middle that rides on top of the wearer's head, in addition to the band that goes around your head, to support the weight of the dinosaur and its electronics.

I like that the unit comes with AAA batteries installed. Just pull out the plastic strip that keeps the unit shut off in its package, and it's ready to go. The original batteries probably won't last long, so plan to replace them, preferably with NiMH rechargeables, if you or your young explorers will be using the headlamp much.

This lamp is intended to be a functional novelty, something between a toy and a tool. It doesnt have the brightest light or the most durable housing, among available headlamps, and I'd advise against testing its ability to resist water, especially submersion. The roaring noise could be annoying if someone is trying to use the lamp in a dark room or tent when others are trying to sleep. I do wish that there was some way to turn off the sound. The sound effects may be useful, though, for parents keeping tabs on their young explorer's nighttime activities.

The colorful stripes and loud roar are fanciful embellishments that will likely appeal to young explorers, but I doubt that anyone would defend them as accurate or realistic. Neither of those features are preserved in the fossil record that we have for dinosaurs, so we probably can't say they are inaccurate, either. The thing is intended to fun. Just go with it.

Let me know if anything in my review was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift

Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange This is a great way to carry extra ammo for your concealed carry weapon. They are easy to load, lie flat in your pocket, and easy to take out when reloading. It sure beats using a bulky speed loader. Yes, the speed loader is quicker, but your chances of needing more than eight shots to defend yourself is minimal.

Eight shots you ask? I bit the bullet (so to speak) and purchased a Smith and Wesson .357 Magnum Model 327 Performance Center, an eight shot revolver. It is a scandium snub nose that holds .38 specials, 38 + P, and .357 magnums. Light but bulky, it fits my large hands well and the recoil (even under full magnum loads) is manageable. Expensive but unique, it is a gun that will become a collector item in the future. Not many revolvers can hold eight large bullets.

And yes, it is a wheel gun for personal protection. My first gun purchase 41 years ago was a Ruger Blackhawk in .44 magnum, carried while salmon fishing in Alaska. I also own a Smith and Wesson .44 magnum Alaskan, another snub nose revolver. So recoil isn't an issue for me. Why a revolver instead of one of the excellent semi autos out there? If I ever need to use it to protect myself or my family, I need to know that it will go BANG when I pull the trigger. I also need to know that my spouse can use it without fumbling around.. Just aim it and pull the trigger. And then again, and again. The simplicity and "bullet proof" action inspires confidence -- especially when you find yourself in a very stressful situation.

My backup piece is also a revolver that will handle the same three calibers. Just in case. Kinda like wearing a belt and suspenders. Redundancy is not a bad thing in personal protection.
text_fidelity_b: Tuff Products QuickStrips Reloading Strips for Revolvers Size 6357 Orange

But I just happened to be washing my car and noticed the nut and washer on the pivoting bold at the bottom was missing. This is extremely dangerous. Had I loaded my bike or bikes up and overlooked this then headed out onto the highway I could have easily lost the entire rack with the bikes and all at 60 mph!!  IF YOU ARE GOING TO BUY ONE OF THESE RACKS. Realize you are responsible to maintain the rack and keep a close eye on such things. The manufacturer should really redesign this. It's not secure enough. There should be some sort of back up that keeps the rack attached if that one bolt fails or loses the nut. At the end of the day this is a good purchase. text_fidelity_a:
Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike This is a low resistance exercise bike. The design is surprisingly solid, with one major problem: the belts are the wrong size!

This is why most people have torn belts in these things. Belt replacement is a major repair, requiring box/socket wrenches and allens, belt routing and careful tension adjustment and alignment.

The good news is that I figured out what belts do work in this thing:
4PJ610 (the wide belt, this is the same as OEM)
3PJ610 (the narrow belt, this is longer than OEM which was 3PJ584).
You can buy belts from Ametric, that's the only place I found.

You could probably get a shorter wide belt instead, but the combination above works pretty well - if tightened sufficiently, there is quite a bit of resistance in this bike.

The reason you want a longer narrow belt is because the tension adjustment is done on both belts at the same time, and the narrow belt is then overtightened and soon rips. Hope this helps you.

I also discarded all the plastic body parts, it's a naked bike now. After taking this thing apart twice, you'll want to do the same...

I sit on this bike when I work at my height-adjustable desk, sometimes all day.
text_fidelity_b: Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike

text_fidelity_a:
LUMINTOP C01 USB Rechargeable Bicycle Front Light, IP68 Waterproof, Bike Headlight with Super Bright Cree Neutral LED, Road Cycling Safety Flashlight, Easy Install & Quick Release This bike light should be getting a 5 star, but because on the first charge the small cover piece to the input for the charge broke off, we have to drop it to a 4. My wife has been using such tiny charing ports for years (like us all) and she’s very careful. This thing easily popped off and in spite of her dainty skills at repairing such tiny things, cannot get it back on. That’s a minus for us.

But as a tool, it’s great. So if they can fix that flaw in how the port cover is attached, we’d be happy to give it a 5.

It arrived in a nice box (for yourself or a gift) in 3 parts: light, clamp, and charger. She charged right away - after as she pushed the piece in it popped off - and we put it on. She severely broke her foot a couple weeks ago and gets around for the next 3 months on a scooter. But she wants to be able to see at night if she’s moving through the house, or if we are outside, so we thought a bike light might work. It’s perfect for that. It fits on the handles of her scooter as easily as a bike - and we plan on switching it to a bike when she’s recovered. In the mean time, the 3 levels of light mean she can see safely in the house without being disruptive, and she can see safely outside moving to the car or around our home. It’s really easy to clamp and remove - she takes it off when we are in the car so it won’t get broken off. And she can easily pop it back on.

Overall this is a great light and minus the flaw with the port cover, we are really happy with it. That we cannot overlook, however, because there is little doubt that in 12+ weeks on the scooter and future use on the bike, covering the port hole would be a safety issue (rain). So the 4 star has to stay. Happy to have it though.
text_fidelity_b: LUMINTOP C01 USB Rechargeable Bicycle Front Light, IP68 Waterproof, Bike Headlight with Super Bright Cree Neutral LED, Road Cycling Safety Flashlight, Easy Install & Quick Release

Fox 40 Tide Rider Multi Sports Referee's Electronic 3 Tone Push Button Whistle The whistle worked fine, bought it 4 years ago. The original battery actually lasted longer than the energizer battery that replaced it. It was loud enough for elementary aged students to hear, but the sound is very direct and therefore doesn't seem as loud as either of my fox 40 whistles (I have a classic and a pearl).
Fast forward to having to really use this whistle due to covid 19 concerns. The off switch is helpful (don't know if that is on other e-whistles) as I forgot to turn it off and it started sounding in my bag when the button was pressed by the contents of the bag.
Why I'm looking for another e-whistle is because when I tried to change the battery, the negative terminal that takes the battery broke. I have a bone to pick with energizer no doubt, but now I'm searching for an e-whistle with a less difficult battery changing process.
